key_insight: A linear eddy-viscosity model can regularize the chaotic adjoint dynamics in wall turbulence, enabling stable prediction of the mean domain of dependence of wall-stress measurements.
engineering_relevance: This improves how we infer past near-wall flow events from sensors, which is useful for flow diagnostics, control, and reconstruction in turbulent channels.
method: Solve adjoint Navier–Stokes equations backward in time from a wall-stress measurement kernel.
Add a linear eddy-viscosity closure to the ensemble-averaged adjoint equations to model the mean DOD.
Compare predicted mean DOD against ensemble-averaged realizations and analyze its Reynolds-number behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct computation of the mean DOD and comparison with the ensemble average, along with universal DOD/DOI behavior across Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: The closure is applied to ensemble-averaged adjoint dynamics, so individual realizations can still exhibit exponential backward-time growth and chaotic sensitivity.
paper_title: Mitigating adjoint chaos in wall turbulence
